newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran invites Iraq to Islamic summit.
newsitem.headline: Iran invites Iraq to Islamic summit.

text.p: An Iranian envoy to Baghdad delivered an invitation to Iraq to attend an Organisation of Islamic Conference summit which Tehran plans to host in December, Iran radio reported on Friday.
It said Health Minister Ali Ridha Mirandi, who arrived in Baghdad on Thursday, relayed the invitation to Iraq's Foreign Minister Mohammad Said al-Sahhaf.
Mirandi is also the personal envoy of Iranian President Ali Hashemi Rafsanjani.

Iranian envoys have in the past three months delivered invitations to Moslem heads of states to attend the OIC summit, but it was not clear from the radio report wether Iran's invitation to Iraq was addressed to President Saddam Hussein.

Saddam's presence at the summit of the Moslem world's biggest body could face reservations by some Gulf Arab leaders, mainly Kuwait which was invaded and occupied by Iraqi troops for seven months in 1990-1991.
Iraq and Iran, two major Gulf powers and old enemies who fought the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran War, are locked on a set of issues which hinder normal ties between them such as prisoners of war.
Diplomats said Rafsanjani's despatch of the health minister to Baghdad was aimed at displaying a humanitarian gesture towards Iraq.
